title: Finite-Tor internal-Hom finiteness over an arbitrary ground field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $n\geq1$. Put $A=R/\varpi^n$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use the constant ring sheaf $A_X$ and the ordinary derived category of $A_X$-module sheaves. Let $K,M\in D^b_c(X,A)$ in the sense of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Assume both have finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]: for each of $K,M$ there is a finite interval of integers containing the cohomology of its derived tensor product with every $A_X$-module sheaf placed in degree zero. Then the ambient ringed-site derived internal Hom
$$R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(K,M)$$
[def-pur-derived-internal-hom] belongs to $D^b_c(X,A)$. In particular it has bounded constructible cohomology with finite stalks and bounded constructible etale origin. The field $k$ may have characteristic zero and need not be perfect or separably closed.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13 (Internal Hom), p. 57, with coefficient ring R replaced by the finite local ring O_E/varpi^n, and its nilpotent maximal ideal; Definition 6.5.1 and the finite-coefficient comparison in the paragraph immediately following it, p. 49. Finite-type schemes over any field are quasi-excellent and ell-coprime. The finite-Tor hypotheses retain the perfect-on-strata condition of D_cons. No Stacks tag states this whole finiteness result.

proof.text: The coefficient quotient A is finite by the proved coefficientExtensionFinite API of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Finite type over the field makes X locally Noetherian by the Mathlib scheme instance; quasi-compactness makes it Noetherian. Convert finite support in Z to an ordered finite cohomological interval using minimum and maximum of lower and upper bounds. No characteristic or separable-closedness hypothesis is introduced.

proof.text: Let P be the intrinsic bounded-constructible object property on the ambient derived category. Use [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] for closure under isomorphisms and triangles. For a retract B of D, functoriality of each homology functor makes H^q(B) a retract of H^q(D). Zero retracts vanish, so the nonzero support is a subset of the finite support of D. Constructibility is preserved by the kernel of 1-ir; the proved retract helper in [det-sf-flat-model-generation] uses [lem-weil-constructible-coefficient-serre]. Translate coefficient-sized constructibility to the intrinsic convention by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-constructibility] and the proved comparison helper in the Serre module. Thus P is thick.

proof.text: Fix M and let F:D(X,A)^op -> D(X,A) send B to RHom(B,M). Equip F with the signed shift structure and triangulated-functor instance supplied by [lem-coef-signed-derived-internal-hom-exact]. The inverse image of P under F, followed by unop, is triangulated. It is retract-stable because any functor sends a retract to a retract and P is retract-stable. This proves that the good first inputs form a thick object property Q.

proof.text: For G the exact locally closed finite-projective generator property of [det-sf-flat-model-generation], the new generator calculation [lem-per-locally-closed-projective-hom-any-field] gives G <= Q, using only the constructibility part of the hypothesis on M. Transport across generator isomorphisms with F.mapIso. Translate the hypothesis on K to coefficient-sized constructibility and an ordered cohomological interval as above. The thick-generation equality of [det-sf-flat-model-generation] places K in G.triangEnvelope. The universal property triangEnvelope_le_iff now places K in Q. This proves intrinsic bounded constructibility of RHom(K,M).
